*Scenario:*

# Go to core-builder application package, select any application and click “Change”
# Click “Add new configuration”
# Fill in the form with “live” package data (e.g. Environment: live, Package: somepkgname) and click “Save” → under the hood this also automagically assignes live cluster to the package
# On the same form change “live” to “prelive” and click “Save” again to create second “prelive” package

The expected behaviour is that a second prelive package is going to be created, but in reality, second save changes the existing “live” package to prelive without removing existing cluster mapping (that maps the package to a live cluster).

+This behavior won’t be possible in the Unicorn Builder. Once core builder is deprecated, this task is going to be resolved.+

{code:sql}with base as (
select
	distinct support_case_id 
from pii.support_case_comments_v2
where 1=1
	and user_type = 'admin_user'
	and lower(comment) = 'nrn'
	and date(created) >= date('2023-10-01')
),
base_curated as (
select 
	a.support_case_id
	, b.user_persona
	, b.created as case_created_utc
	, c.country_code 
from base as a
left join ng_customer_support.etl_tw_support_case as b
	on a.support_case_id = b.id 
	and b.user_persona in ('driver', 'rider', 'fleet_owner', 'driver_lead', 'business_company')
left join ng_public.admin_system_city as c
	on b.city_id = c.id 
where 1=1
	and date(b.created_date) >= date('2023-10-01')
	and date(b.created_date) < date('2023-11-01')
),
agent_replies as (
select
	support_case_id
	, count(event_id) as count_agent_replies
from pii.support_case_comments_v2
where 1=1
	and user_type = 'admin_user'
	and is_public = true
	and date(created) >= date('2023-10-01')
	and user_id not in (10030)
group by 1)
select 
	d.case_created_utc
	, d.country_code
	, d.user_persona
	, d.support_case_id
	, e.count_agent_replies
	, g.issue_title 
from base_curated as d
left join agent_replies as e	
	on d.support_case_id = e.support_case_id
left join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case_issue_keys_updated as f
	on d.support_case_id = f.support_case_id 
left join ng_customer_support.support_issue_store_support_issue as g
	on f.issue_key = g.issue_key 
	and g.is_internal = false{code}

It might be possible due to a day-end ride, usually, the orders finished at midnight are added to the next day’s balance, as the balance calculation is based on the time stamp.

This causes a time difference between the payout system and the balance system. However, the balance and the payout is correct. It is only a discrepancy in the reporting. Most importantly they have received this difference in the next payout.

Please check the new [view balance|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/balance?filter=%7B%22limit%22%3A25%2C%22offset%22%3A0%2C%22filter%22%3A%7B%22start_date_ts%22%3A1696197600%2C%22end_date_ts%22%3A1696802400%2C%22types%22%3A%5B%22ride_hailing_fleet%22%5D%2C%22external_id%22%3A67889%7D%7D&tz=Europe%2FTallinn] to check the correctness of the payout.

And please check the [record|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/records?recordFilter=%7B%22action_timestamp_from%22%3A1696197600%2C%22action_timestamp_to%22%3A1696802400%2C%22from_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22from_agent_id%22%3A67889%2C%22agent_filter_operator%22%3A%22OR%22%2C%22to_agent_type%22%3A%22fleet%22%2C%22to_agent_id%22%3A67889%7D&page=%7B%22limit%22%3A100%2C%22offset%22%3A0%7D] of the end days of Sunday (in this example will be a different timezone because of my location)

!Screenshot 2023-11-10 at 13.29.25.png|width=1645,height=657!

So this amount just capture in the balance before the payout, but this amount will be included in the next payout

_Clause 61_

_During the inspection, the inspector can take statements from representatives of supervised legal and natural persons, as well as from participants caught in the surveillance and/or other persons caught at the place of inspection, witnesses who, at his request, are obliged to give statements with accurate details important for establishing the facts in possession inspection supervision._

Hi, [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2]! Coming back on this topic as we received a reply from the external counsel. After discussing the reply with [~accountid:62d7b457807cf6f78ca9d117], we see there 3 options to proceed further:

# Full compliance - To fully comply with the local legislation we need to allow users to subscribe if they refuse to consent to the provision of services during the withdrawal period, but not to provide them with any services during the subscription period. For this we need a separate page on the app with the pre-agreed consent wording and possibility to subscribe without giving the consent.
# Partial compliance (consent given by accepting T&Cs) - We can incorporate the consent into our T&Cs and say that by subscribing to our T&Cs the user agrees to the provision of services during the withdrawal period. This means that user will automatically give consent and will not be able to subscribe without giving such consent. This can be considered as “unfair commercial practice” and will have the same repercussions as described in option 3. The external counsel recommended to separate giving the consent to the provision of services during the withdrawal period and consent to T&Cs application. 
# Partial compliance (consent on a separate page in the app, no possibility to subscribe without giving consent) - We can add a separate page on the app requesting the user to consent to the provision of services during the withdrawal period and not allow the user to subscribe without giving a consent. We would use this part of the pre-agreed wording: “_By pressing “Agree” I confirm that I want to start using the Bolt Plus subscription benefits right away, even if it is still within the first 14 days when I can change my mind and cancel._“. The external counsel believes this will be considered as an “unfair commercial practice” and may have the following consequences if the local authority will investigate the issue *due to a complaint filed by a user* (but there is a slight chance that they will start investigation on their own):
## By breaching the local act a fine of up to 331,94 € may be imposed for an offence.
## By breaching the local act or consumer protection provisions of EU legislation a fine up to 66,400 € may be imposed. Where the breach recurs within 12 months the authority shall impose a fine up to 166,000 €. 
## Where, despite the imposition of a fine, within the period of 12 months we repeatedly unduly prevent, unreasonably inhibit or otherwise frustrate the exercise of the consumer’s right of withdrawal, such conduct shall be regarded as a particularly serious breach of our obligation and therefore the Trades Licensing Office may cancel our trade authorisation. 

We think that the likelihood of being pursued by the authority is not that great because it is not in the users' interest to subscribe and wait for 14 days before they can start using the service, but the possibility still exists and we need to be cautious in case we will use partially complying solution and be ready to implement changes if needed so as not to be burdened by high fines and not to lose our right to operate in SK.

Current usage of the Verification SDK from the {{gateway}} service [happens|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/rides/integration/gateway/main/service/IdentityVerificationService.ts#L25] in {{/getLocationConfig}}. The list required flows is collated from {{city_compliance_config}} and {{country_compliance_config}} dynamic config arrays. Then for each flow name on the list the status of the flow is checked:

* the passed flows are skipped
* the not-yet-started flows are triggered, making them pending
* the list of all pending flows is returned to FE in the response (combination of just-started and already-pending)

The flow status is retrieved/stored by a combination of {{userId + flowName}}.

FE shows the actual flow to the user and then reports the results using Verification SDK public endpoint (not sure which, probably {{/verification/flowRun/submitData}}).

Hello Yulia, 

The fraud team recently introduced a feature called “keep pre-authorization”, this feature was meant to help reduce fraud rates and has largely been very successful. 

A pre-authorisation amount is held at the start of the trip. At the end of the trip if the amount changed the fraud team determines whether to keep this amount already held at the beginning or cancel the pre-authorisation and attempt to capture the full amount. If fraud decides to keep the pre-authorisation amount the remaining amount is added to the balance of the user

You can find a lot more information here about the project;

[https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3763241069/A+lost+pre-authorization+problem#Keep-pre-authorisation-and-put-rest-to-the-balance|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3763241069/A+lost+pre-authorization+problem#Keep-pre-authorisation-and-put-rest-to-the-balance|smart-link] 

However regarding the customer complaint, we’ve always charged a pre-auth amount that can differ from the estimated price. The amount we charge for the pre-auth is completely determined by the fraud team depending on the risk profile of the user.

The only difference in this trip is that we choose to keep pre-authorised amount rather than attempt to capture the full payment. 

I hope this helps your understanding of how this process works. Please note that while we can explain how the keep pre-auth process works we do not give information on why and when it is applied to a trip to clients.

Regards,

''

anbei auszugsweise der Einsatzbericht.

Im vorliegenden Fall muss geklärt werden, ob der Beschuldigte sich tatsächlich per App auf Ihrem Mietgerät eingewählt hat, da er mutmaßlich Ihr Mietgerät im öffenntlichen Straßenverkehr unter erheblichen Alkoholeinfluss geführt haben soll und zweimal vom Gehweg mit dem Fahrzeug auf die Straße fiel, so dass weitere Verkehrsteilnehmer diesen beinahe erfasst hätte. Der Beschuldigte behauptet, dass er das Mietgerät nicht geführt hätte, sondern lediglich „geschoben“ habe.

Die Angaben sind erforderlich, da es zu einer Fahrerlaubnisbeschlagnahme gekommen ist.

Sollten Sie sich nicht in der Lage sehen, die angeforderten Daten zu übermitteln, so wird ein staatsanwaltschaftliches Auskunftsersuchen beantragt.

Einsatzbericht

# Allgemeines Am Samstag, den 21.10.2023, um 21:33 Uhr, erhält die Funkstreifenwagenbesatzung PK Breves und PKin Doelfs (Unterzeichnerin) einen Einsatz auf der Kreuzung Windmühlenbergstraße/Nord-Süd-Straße in 38259 Salzgitter-Bad. Dort soll es zu einer Nutzung eines Elektrokleinstfahrzeuges durch zwei männliche, augenscheinlich betrunkene Personen gekommen sein.
# Feststellungen vor Ort Vor Ort treffen die eingesetzten Beamten an der Ecke Windmühlenbergstraße/ Friedrich-Ebert-Straße auf zwei männliche Personen. Während des Eintreffens der Beamten stellt einer der beiden Männer einen E-Scooter auf dem angrenzenden Gehweg ab und fotografiert diesen daraufhin mit Blitzlicht mit seinem Smartphone. Dabei handelt es sich um den A. W. Neben Herrn W. kann vor Ort Herr D.P. angetroffen werden. Den beiden anwesenden Personen wurde der Vorhalt erläutert, dass soeben zwei männliche Personen, deren Personenbeschreibung mit ihrem äußeren Erscheinungsbild übereinstimmt, gemeinsam mit einem E-Scooter die Windmühlenbergstraße entlang gefahren seien und dabei mehrfach gestürzt seien.
# Angaben des Zeugen Durch die Funkstreifenwagenbesatzung POK Kurs/ PK Reinink wurde der MELZE C. G. aufgesucht. Näheres siehe Vermerk durch PK Reinink.
# Angaben des Beschuldigten Basierend auf den Angaben des Zeugen kann der anwesende Herr W. anhand einer Personenbeschreibung zweifelsfrei als Führer des Elektrokleinstfahrzeuges identifiziert werden. Nach einer verstandenen Belehrung als Beschuldigter in einem Strafverfahren gibt Herr W. an, dass er sich gemeinsam mit dem ebenfalls anwesenden Herrn P. von seiner Wohnanschrift in 38259 Salzgitter-Bad zu dem Restaurant seines Bruders (Hinter dem Salze 1A, 38259 Salzgitter-Bad) habe begeben wollen. Dabei seien die beiden noch vor seiner Wohnanschrift auf den E-Scooter mit dem Versicherungskennzeichen 427-BVI gestoßen und haben diesen für den bevorstehenden Weg nutzen wollen. Weiterhin gibt er an, dass sie zwar versucht hätten den E-Scooter zu nutzen, dies jedoch nicht funktioniert habe und er demnach den E-Scooter nicht geführt habe. Herr W. erklärt, dass er die App, die er für eine Anmeldung an dem E-Scooter benötigen würde, nicht habe und dieser daher lediglich eine Störmeldung in Form von einem Piepton gemeldet habe. Während der ersten Befragung kann durch die Unterzeichnerin ein Alkoholgeruch sowie ein unsicherer Stand bei dem Beschuldigten wahrgenommen werden. Auf Nachfrage gibt Herr W. an, dass er zuvor gemeinsam mit Herrn P. Bier konsumiert habe. Eine genaue Angabe über die Menge könne er nicht machen. Ein freiwilliger Atemalkoholtest ergab eine Atemalkoholkonzentration von 1,85 Promille. Infolgedessen wurde durch die Unterzeichnerin eine Blutentnahme angeordnet.''

”Persoana fizica autorizata” or “PFA” is one of the smallest businesses someone can have in Romania. A PFA business can have a minimum of 1 employee (the owner) and a maximum of 4 employees (including the owner). 

It was incorrectly translated by my colleague to English as “AUTHORIZED NATURAL PERSON”, although the closest equivalent I find is “Self employed individual”. 
However, the user requested the data in Romanian, and it can be added to the invoices as such: 

Bumbu Răzvan Iliuță PERSOANĂ FIZICĂ AUTORIZATĂ
CUI 48786205

[~accountid:5bc4571d505b7a135722281f] please provide the requested data to the authorities.

Under the law Operational Activities Law the operational activities measures shall be performed according to the *general method*, if the tactics, form and scope of their performance do not significantly infringe the fundamental rights of persons (Art.7.2). Investigatory questioning shall be performed *by questioning persons regarding facts in which the bodies performing operational activities are interested* (Art.9.1). Thus, the law permits the authorities to collect general information without disclosing the specific purpose. 

In the request letter sent by the authorities, it is states that “We confirm that the information received will be used for operational work and *the protection of personal data will be ensure*”. 

Although I agree that the request may not be sufficiently precise from the GDPR standpoint, as the purpose is not clearly provided, and the request is not limited in time, we must pay due regard to the provisions of Operational Activities law and the confirmation of the authorities that the data will be processed in accordance with data protection laws. Unfortunately, we cannot solely impose our own vision of how the request should be formulated, as it may lead to a negative deterioration in our relationships with authorities. Thus, we need to find a more balanced and flexible approach when reviewing authority requests, tolerating some reasonable deviation from the ideal request we have in mind.

- Now when we get a new request, [we block creating a new tab/newPage in Chrome (3minute exactly)|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/platform/commerce/invoicing_pdf/main/service/PdfService.ts#L20] after that puppeteer throws `{{ProtocolError: Target. create a target timed out.}}  

- Due to chrome disconnection, the pod is alive and active with no chrome process running in the background, therefore every request fails with the timeout.


----


Discussed with the Pint Team possible fixes to mitigate this issue, and below are the proposed fixes.

1. Re-instantiate the new Chrome connection on the browser disconnect. (I’ve coded and tested this on pre-live. looks fine)

2. Shut down the service on disconnect, so that Kubernetes can start a new pod with the already chrome process being running on service startup.

Need to investigate why the Chrome process is getting killed,  [ticket|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PIF-1241?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiZTdkZjRjZTcxNzkxNDZlNjgzZmMzMjNhMWI3YzllZmQiLCJwIjoiaiJ9] for the same to the PINT Team.

[~accountid:6052891960d39e006f72f0f0] just two follow-up comments that might be helpful:

* 3.3. is Romanian specific. Art. 3 (1) e) of the UTP Directive has a local addition, reading a such "the buyer requires the supplier to pay for the deterioration or loss, or both, of agricultural and food products that occurs on the buyer's premises or after ownership has been transferred to the buyer, where such deterioration or loss is not caused by the negligence or fault of the supplier. *By way of exception, for agricultural and food products affected by non-visible alterations, the supplier will cover the replacement cost*." This would be read, per a contrario, that the buyer may not charge additional penalties to the replacement cost.
* As regards 11.3, under the Romanian Civil Code, the parties to contract may invoke hardship, unless expressly excluded (which is the purpose of 11.3). This is not necessarily Romanian specific, except to the end that hardship under Romanian law is statutory and intended to cover cases in which unforeseen events occur that fundamentally alter the equilibrium of a contract resulting in an excessive burden being placed on one of the parties involved (i.e. in other jurisdictions the contract must expressly provide a hardship clause, under Romanian law it is automatically applicable if not excluded). In the Global Supplier Contract, the seller could invoke hardship saying that it may no longer provide the products at the agreed price, and ask for a renegotiation. We assumed that this protects Bolt, as prices tend to increase, thereby putting the supplier in a more probable situation to invoke hardship.

Otherwise - all good to accept the changes and share the template.

Thank you!

Instead of trying to play with data intervals that get read and written within one model run, it might make sense to calculate the ranks separately.

Options:

* Preferred - manager’s would have a to do task in their inbox. See below for more details.
* Secondary option - manager’s will receive a notification. See below for more details.

----

Option 1 - preferred: To do task for managers

Managers will receive a to do task to their inbox (similar to the task that Getter receives when someone is leaving and their options need to be terminated; when someone is going on a long term leave, and their options vesting should be suspended).

!Screenshot 2023-11-13 at 13.11.59.png|width=877,height=478!

To do task needs to be in place individually - for each individual the manager will receive a separate task.

In this task there’s an overview what they are expected to do, with guides to Manager’s Playbook (hyperlinked).

To get the task “done” they need to submit the task. Similar to “job profile request” process manager needs to add a “resolution”. Options from the drop down list could be the following:

* i’ve made a separate grant request
* i’m not planning on requesting additional units
* other

With the latter two options it should be mandatory for managers to add a comment which would clarify their decision.

----

Option 2: Notification to managers

# First notification to manager 3 months before someone from their team is fully vesting their grant
# Second notification to manager 1,5 months before someone from their team is fully vesting their grant - only if manager hasn’t initiated stock request after the first notification
# Third notification to manager 2 weeks before someone from their team is fully vesting their grant - only if manager hasn’t initiated stock request after the first and second notification 

If the “rule” cannot be met (that 2nd and 3rd notification would only be sent out if manager hasn’t initiated the request so far) then might need to rethink how often and when to send out notifications.

NB! If we would have to go with Option 2: notifications; instead of Option 1: to do task, then People Partners should be excluded from this notification, see next section

----

New request: Report to PP’s and Total Rewards team (mainly to the security that is connected with my accesses, stock partner etc). 

Report should reflect employees who are about to fully vest their units in the upcoming 3 months. 

It should include columns like: Employee ID, worker, country location, job profile, manager, supervisory org, grant details that is about to be fully vested (grant ID, amount of units, grant date, vested as of date)

Additionally it should reflect whether to do task has been sent out to manager, and if manager has submitted the task then with what resolution.

----

upd: external counsels information 



# *Whether Bolt is caught up by the Freedom of Information Act*

 

Our view is that the UK Freedom of Information Act 2000 ("*FOIA*") does +not+ apply to Bolt. The FOIA only applies to public authorities/bodies or those that are wholly owned by the Crown, the wider public sector or both. In particular, [Schedule 1|https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2000/36/schedule/1] of the FOIA provides a list of public bodies that would be captured by the FOIA (none of which would capture Bolt). Note that there are some other exceptions for other bodies (e.g. health practitioners) but, again, these would not apply to Bolt.



# *Whether this can also be treated as the DSR request*

 

We understand that the passenger has made a request under the FOIA specifically, and not under data protection legislation. In addition, looking at the information requested, we also understand that there is no indication that the passenger has specifically asked for access to their personal data.

 

+However+, a data subject access request does not need to include phrases such as 'subject access request', 'right of access' or 'Article 15 UK GDPR'. Provided that it is clear that the passenger is requesting access to their own personal data, this is sufficient for the request to be treated as a data subject access request. In addition, the ICO guidance on this point highlights that it is not uncommon for a request to mistakenly state that it is a request under the FOIA (as may be the case in the present scenario). In these circumstances, where the request relates to the passenger's personal data, Bolt must treat it as a subject access request under Article 15 UK GDPR.

 

With this in mind, we understand that the passenger has requested the following information:

 

·         Crash Investigation Report for the incident

·         Complaints Policy and Procedures

·         Details of your insurers

·         Crash Investigation Policy and Procedures

·         Information as to the action taken for the driver

 

Bolt should therefore look to identify and confirm whether any of the documents/information above contains any of the passenger's personal data. On the face of it, it appears to be unlikely, for example, that Bolt's Complaints Policy and Procedures would contain any such personal data – however, if documents such as the Crash Investigation Report for the incident includes the passenger's personal data, the request should be treated as a subject access request for that particular element of disclosure. 

 

# *How should Bolt respond in this regard and which information are we entitled to not provide?*

 

Under UK data protection legislation, Bolt is not required to disclose any of the documents/information above to the extent that it does not include any of the passenger's personal data. However, as per the answer to Q2 above, if Bolt identifies any personal data in the documents/information requested above it would need to treat that element of the request as a subject access request – in this scenario, note that the passenger would only be entitled to access their own personal data (not whole documents or personal data of other individuals unless consent is obtained from such other individuals or it would be reasonable to do so without obtaining consent).

 

In the first instance, we recommend that Bolt should confirm whether any of the documents/information requested includes the passenger's personal data. Subject to the outcome of this, Bolt can respond in one of the two following ways:

 

# *If the documents/information requested does* 

+not+ contain any personal data of the passenger, respond to the passenger explaining that the FOIA does not apply to Bolt and therefore Bolt is not under any obligation under the FOIA to disclose the documents requested. In this response, Bolt can also consider confirming that none of the documents/information requested includes any of the passenger's personal data.

 

# If the documents/information requested contains personal data of the passenger, respond to the passenger to: (1) explain that the FOIA does not apply to Bolt; (2) explain that Bolt can consider the documents/information requested by the passenger in the context of a subject access request under Article 15 UK GDPR, but that this only entitles the passenger to personal data about them and not other individuals (such as the driver); and (3) clarify whether the passenger would like to receive their personal data contained in the documents/information requested and if so, treat the request as a data subject access request and provide a copy of the passenger's personal data contained within any of the documents/information requested with redactions where appropriate.   



# *What is the timeline for the response to this request?*

 

If there is no personal data of the passenger contained in the documents/information requested, there would be no obligation for Bolt to respond in the first place and therefore no timelines would apply.

 

However, to the extent that personal data are contained in the documents/information requested, the usual subject access request timeframes would apply under data protection legislation (i.e. responding within one month of receipt of the request with the option to extent to up to two months for requests subject to Bolt having appropriate justifications to do so e.g. complex requests, which is unlikely to be the case in this scenario).



# *Other important information in this regard.*

We understand that Bolt drivers are likely to be self-employed and therefore they may be responsible for obtaining their own insurance. However, subject to what Bolt's privacy policy for drivers states, Bolt may or may not be able to disclose information relating to the driver's insurance policy to passengers. In any event, if it wishes to do so, Bolt could consider: (1) reminding the driver to notify their insurers; and (2) subsequently sending a short response to the passenger to let him/her know that Bolt have done this. This may help manage Bolt's relationship with the passenger.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

This need to to be calculated for the month activity from 1st until 31st data, but you was referencing on the weekly report.

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

Before going into specific cases highlighting, that there are no by default grants happening - each grant needs to be requested, approved by different parties and once this is done, request is being processed according to our monthly process.

If there are any future job changes, promotions etc then employees total compensation shall be reviewed during that. Likewise with job changes and promotions, also with [refresh grants|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BMP/pages/4427186625/Equity+Compensation#Grant-refresh-(replacing-fully-vested-grant)], if any additional grant is relevant then it’s the manager’s responsibility to make sure that everything would be processed in a timely manner in WD. HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

Ladies and Gentlemen

I refer to the Swiss Code of Criminal Procedure (StPO), according to which, according to Article 12 lit.

According to Article 263 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, items and assets belonging to an accused person can be confiscated if they are used as evidence. This also includes data. According to Art. 265, the owner of the data is obliged to hand over the data. If the request to hand over the data is ignored, criminal proceedings can be initiated according to Art. 292 of the Criminal Code or a fine can be imposed.

In criminal proceedings, the DSG (Federal Data Protection Act) does not apply, only the Swiss Code of Criminal Procedure.

Since Switzerland is not in the European Union, the GDPR is not applicable here. I refer to Articles 2 and 3 of the GDPR.

Thank you for taking note of.

Best regards

Sonja Meier

h3. {color:#36b37e}*Data analysis insights:*{color}

*Handling time*

* AHT result is on target, all markets that have high incoming volumes of this issue, have healthy AHT results. AHT is higher only in the markets where the sample size was very low. 
* *High AHT:* when reviewing the tickets it was noticed that higher AHT is usually caused by quality issues, e.g. agents asking a lot of unnecessary questions (that are not documented in the process), asking for needed information in separate messages instead of asking everything in one, etc. 
* *Low AHT:* it was noticed that many tickets with low AHT are about pre-auth. This situation has its own issue tag and a process, however, if the customer considers pre-auth as an unknown charge, then the unknown charge tag is added. Supportability team also knows that the majority of “I have an unknown charge” cases are about pre-auth ([Confluence|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SUPP/pages/3742466081/I+have+an+unknown+charge+02.22]). 

*CSAT*

* 26/35 markets have CSAT results below the target (<80%).
* Out of 55 tickets checked for CSAT, 71% were about pre-auth, 16% were about charges that were forgotten and only 13% were actual unknown charges.
* Good and Bad rated tickets are very similar, the rating depends on how the customer reacts to pre-auth.
* Dissatisfaction is mostly caused by:
** Pre-auth not being released immediately; 
** Pre-auth in general;
** Actual unknown charges - no help from CS due to the current process.

Adding some notes from calls we’ve had with the provider team:

* Regular providers can show a spinning wheel before polling returns a calculated ETA, so it’s fine for them to wait until events are propagated in the backend through Timing, and an ETA calculation is sent to Order polling.
* Integrators don’t use polling, so they need the ETA calculated synchronously on the call that returns a created order info + the call that marks the provider preparation start.
** The event that triggers an ETA calculation is fired after the order creation call is finished, so an ETA calculation cannot be made available through polling before this call finishes.
** The solution then is to compute on demand an ETA both at order creation and at provider acceptance, and return it to the integrators.
* Delivery-eta will implement a new endpoint that calculates these ETAs on demand, basically replacing the current endpoints {{computeEtaAtOrderCreation}} and {{predictPreparationTimeWithDelay}}. 
** This new endpoint will be called by {{delivery-provider-pos}}, after the call to {{/internal/getOrdersByIds}} and will augment the result with the fields {{expected_time_when_preparation_is_ready_in_seconds}} and 
{{expected_timestamp_when_preparation_is_ready}}.
** For choosing the new endpoint semantics, we should take into account how it will fit into the larger picture of Centralise ETA, for example there might be a need for new endpoints that will return pre-calculated ETAs.
** Also, an optional check is to see if this new endpoint can be replaced for all the flows where currently {{computeEtaAtOrderCreation}} and {{predictPreparationTimeWithDelay}} are used.

As a result of the mystery driver assessment, Bolt will offer incentives to well-scoring drivers and will permanently or temporarily block drivers who are reported by the mystery rivers to have committed certain behaviours/acts.

IMO, this project +would increase the risk of reclassification+ because, by monitoring the quality of the service provided and imposing sanctions on drivers (i.e. temporary and permanent blocks) Bolt would be exercising one of the typical employer powers that Paraguayan courts take into account when deciding whether a driver should be considered an employee rather than self-employed.

In addition, a bill that aims to establish an automatic presumption of employment for drivers providing services through digital platforms is currently being debated in the Paraguayan Parliament. It has not yet been decided whether the law will be passed or not, as well as the requirements or criteria that will determine the presumption of employment, but the imposition of sanctions will certainly be one of those criteria.

In view of the above, I would not, in principle, recommend going ahead with the Mystery Rider Project.

(4) An explanation pursuant to subsection (3) may not be requested from a person who would thereby breach a duty of confidentiality expressly imposed or recognised by law, unless he has been released from that duty by the competent authority or by the person in whose interest he is under that duty. As discussed during our meeting, since the actions will only affect a few drivers each week (if even) then we can test the procedure based on the following assumptions and recommendations: 

* *Only assess complaints directly referring to driver behaviour*: You will only act in relation to drivers with the lowest ratings, you will review each individual driver and assess if there are several complaints which are not covered by the Driver Score. It will be a case by case assessment of the overall circumstances. We are only expecting very few drivers to even be covered by this review. It is important that only complaints are considered which are +directly in relation to driver behaviou+r and not related to aspects out of the driver’s control e.g. heavy traffic, platform issues etc. 
* *Transparency*: as discuss it is important that the driver is informed why the driver has been blocked. The drivers needs to understand what they can do in order to prevent any future blocking. 
* *Warning*: We +strongly recommend+ that you include a warning to the driver before any blockings are taking place, this will limit our reclassification risk as the driver then has direct information on complaints and can mitigate the bad behaviour prior to Bolt taking any action. 
* *Appeal process*: Currently the possibility to appeal the decision is only mentioned in the permanent blocking scenario, this should be an option in relation to all blockings even if they are short-term. 

If we see an increase in driver complaints due to these blockings, especially in relation to reclassification, then you must flag this to the Legal team as soon as possible. Let me know how it goes and if you have any follow-up questions on this, otherwise I will close this ticket.

*Searching for a wanted person*

(1) The wanted order shall be immediately enforced by the jurisdictional structures of the Ministry of the Administration and Interior that are to perform nationwide activities to identify, search for, locate and apprehend the wanted individual.
*(2) Public entities are under an obligation to provide support, as required by law and according to their legal authority, to the police who are searching for a wanted individual.*
(3) The activity of searching for a individual for the purpose of placing them on pre-trial arrest, carried out by the police, shall be supervised by prosecutors especially appointed from the prosecutor’s office attached to the Court of Appeals in whose jurisdiction the court is located that tried the motion for pre- trial custody warrant on the merits. When the pre-trial custody warrant was returned in a case under the jurisdiction of the Prosecutor General’s Office, supervision of the search activities shall be the responsibility of the prosecutor who is performing or has performed the criminal investigation in the case.
(4) In the other situations, the activity of searching for wanted individuals shall be supervised by prosecutors especially appointed by the prosecutor’s office attached to the Court of Appeals in whose jurisdiction the enforcement court is located or another court that has jurisdiction under special law.

The invoices don’t reflect the payout, they reflect the commission we charge (and other fees). For provider companies (meaning one umbrella company for their smaller providers), the invoice reflects the sum of all fees of all of their providers - not individually. 

Weekly sales report, on the other hand, is per provider. It reflects the fees and their weekly earnings per provider - individual in each of their own reports. 

The amount paid to the bank account for provider_company is the total amount for all providers, and paid at once every week, as far as I know ([~accountid:616ff0d6702bd0006a685f65] can help us confirm that). *Telecommunications Act (TKG)*
*Section 113 Manual information procedure*

(1) Any person providing or assisting in providing telecommunications services in a business capacity may, in compliance with subsection (2), use the data collected in accordance with sections 95 and 111 in compliance with this provision to meet information obligations vis-à-vis the bodies referred to in subsection (3). This also applies to data by means of which access to terminal equipment or to storage devices or units installed in or physically separated from such terminal equipment is protected. The data to be included in information provided may also be determined using an internet protocol address allocated at a certain point in time; traffic data may also be evaluated by means of automated procedures for this purpose. All internal company data sources are to be taken into account for the provision of information in accordance with sentence 3.

(2) Information may only be provided where a body as referred to in subsection (3) has made an individual request, in text form, for the purpose of prosecuting criminal or administrative offences, averting danger to public safety or order or discharging the legal functions of the bodies referred to in subsection (3) para 3, citing a legal provision allowing the body to collect the data to which reference is made in subsection (1); data as referred to in subsection (1) may not be transmitted to any other public or non-public bodies. In cases of imminent danger, the information may also be provided where the request is made in another form. In this case, the request is to be confirmed in text form subsequently without undue delay. Responsibility for the admissibility of the information request lies with the bodies referred to in subsection (3).

(3) Bodies for the purpose of subsection (1) are

# the authorities responsible for the prosecution of criminal or administrative offences;
# the authorities responsible for averting danger to public safety or order;
# the federal and state authorities for the protection of the Constitution, the Federal Armed Forces Counter-Intelligence Office and the Federal Intelligence Service.

(4) The party providing or assisting in providing telecommunications services in a business capacity is to transmit the data to be provided without undue delay and in full. The persons with obligations shall maintain silence vis-à-vis the parties concerned and third parties about the request for and provision of information.

(5) Any person providing or assisting in providing telecommunications services in a business capacity is to make such arrangements as are required in their area of responsibility for the provision of information, at their own expense. Any person having more than 100,000 customers is to provide, for the receipt of information requests and the provision of the associated information, a secure electronic interface in compliance with the technical directive drawn up in accordance with section 110(3) through which transmission secured against disclosure of the data to unauthorised persons is also guaranteed. In doing so, it shall be ensured that each request for information is verified by a competent specialist for compliance with the formal requirements set out in subsection (2) and that further processing of the request is not allowed before the result of the verification is positive.





----



Section 100j
Subscriber data request

(1) Insofar as it is necessary to establish the facts or determine the whereabouts of an accused person, information may be requested

# on subscriber data pursuant to section 3 no. 6 of the Telecommunications Act and on data collected pursuant to section 172 of the Telecommunications Act (section 174 (1) sentence 1 of the Telecommunications Act) from the person who, on a commercial basis, provides or collaborates in the provision of telecommunications services and

# on subscriber data pursuant to section 2 (2) no. 2 of the Telecommunications and Telemedia Data Protection Act (section 22 (1) sentence 1 of the Telecommunications and Telemedia Data Protection Act) from the person who, on a commercial basis, makes available for use or provides access for the purpose of the use of their own or others’ telemedia.

If the request for information under sentence 1 no. 1 refers to data by means of which access to terminal equipment or to storage media installed in such terminal equipment or physically separate therefrom are protected (section 174 (1) sentence 2 of the Telecommunications Act), then information may only be requested if the statutory requirements for the use of such data are met. If the request for information under sentence 1 no. 2 refers to passwords collected in the form of subscriber data or other data which are used to provide protection against access to end devices or to storage devices which are used in or kept separate from such end devices (section 23 of the Telecommunications and Telemedia Data Protection Act), then a request for information may only be made if the statutory conditions for their use in the prosecution of an especially serious crime under section 100b (2) no. 1 (a), (c), (e), (f), (g), (h) or (m), or no. 3 (b) alternative 1 or no. 5, 6, 9 or 10 are met.

h3. {color:#36b37e}*Features for pre auth improvement*{color}

* [*Pre Auth Communication*|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02CUF8CFCZ/p1692776454455419] feature was rolled out globally on October 20th. 
** *Problem:* One of the top reasons for tickets in our payment experience is the fact that our users don’t understand what is a pre-authorization, especially when the money release from this pre-auth takes hours or days, as it has happened with some banks before.
** *Solution:* As a solution, we have prepared better communications about the pre auth for cases when the pre auth has been done but the order (for whatever reasons) ended up being canceled.
* [*Reuse of initial pre-authorisation in case of not happened ride*|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/4349592624/Reuse+of+initial+pre-authorisation+in+case+of+not+happened+ride.] feature is planned for Q1 2024 ([Slack|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C057S376JA2])
** *Problem*: When the Rider is making the order Fraud team makes a decision to request pre-authorisation.  If the ride did not happen, Payments will release pre-authorisation. Despite Bolt releases money immediately, it might take some time for banks to react and remove the hold from the funds. When the Rider decides to order again then the process of pre-authorisation will take place again. Due to issues with funds release on the banks' side, it might happen that there are several money holds.
** *Solution*: Reuse pre-authorisation for cancelled order for next order. Ideally if price did not change, we can reuse pre-auth for the new order. In case when price is lower it also should work. When the price is higher do the pre-auth adjustment if supported or immediately cancelled it and create a new one.

[~accountid:5d95f00136d2520dde7ede17] the comment form the external adviser:

The order is an order to seize the debtor‘s assets. *This order is mandatory and binding, thus Bolt has to comply with it.*

Bailiffs have rights conferred by law to seize the debtor's assets, including, but not limited to, the debtor’s assets and (or) property rights with the third parties. The issuance and enforcement of such orders are governed by other norms of the Code of Civil Procedure of the Republic of Lithuania than the request to make deductions from salaries (on which we commented previously). In this case, the bailiff issued an order for seizure of debtor‘s assets after receiving the reply form Bolt (prepared according to template). Since one of the arguments of the Bolt‘s response was that the company was not in a position to calculate the exact amount of the deduction from drivers’ payouts, the bailiff issued an order and clarified what actions the company must take, i. e. Bolt must pay all driver‘s commission to the bank account, specified in the order.

The order of seizure, issued by the bailiff, is valid and enforceable. Thus, Bolt must comply with the order. In the case of non-compliance, the company (and its CEO) risks getting a fine of up to 300 EUR/day, as well as a request to compensate losses incurred as a result of non-compliance with such an order.

While there is no exact recipe on how to configure the circuit breaker thresholds, we should start by looking at the endpoints with the most traffic - a view on this is available on [nodemonitor|https://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/a968c700-2167-411d-9957-f4640b38dd02/circuitbreaker-requests-volume?orgId=1&var-team=eater-order-xp&var-type=All&var-host=All&var-shard=All&var-service=All&var-tag=All], see sections [Requests SUM per minute per path|https://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/a968c700-2167-411d-9957-f4640b38dd02/circuitbreaker-requests-volume?orgId=1&var-team=eater-order-xp&var-type=All&var-host=All&var-shard=All&var-service=All&var-tag=All#:~:text=per%20minute%20per-,path,-Last%20*] and [Pay attention on this paths|https://nodemonitor.boltint.net/graph/d/a968c700-2167-411d-9957-f4640b38dd02/circuitbreaker-requests-volume?orgId=1&var-team=eater-order-xp&var-type=All&var-host=All&var-shard=All&var-service=All&var-tag=All#:~:text=attention%20on%20this-,paths,-Last%20*]. 

The goal of this task is to lower the volume threshold of the CB to make sure that the CB works as expected when there is an issue with a service, but still to make the check only if there is enough traffic to be worth to short circuiting the requests (probably it is ok if the volume is not above the threshold during the night).

Together with lowering of the *volume threshold*, the *fail ratio* should be adjusted so that CB don’t open in the case of just a few false positive errors.

[Read more on |https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/2620752402/Circuit+Breaker+-+practical+guide]circuit breakers purpose.

[Example on how to configure CB|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/2116323382/Circuit+Breakers+-+Setup+Example].

The State Service for the Protection of Consumer Rights (hereinafter - the Service) through the Consumer Rights Information System (VTIS) received the request of the user Tomas Leontjev (hereinafter - the User) (reg. no. 7G-6952) on 2023-09-25 and 2023-10-06, 2023 -10-09 additional documents and explanations regarding the undelivered order of the service provider UAB "Bolt Services LT". In the request, the User indicated that through the e-mail of the service provider UAB "Bolt Services LT". the app submitted an order that was to be delivered to the User by UAB "Bolt Services LT" courier. After placing the order, the courier who called the User indicated that he would not deliver the order, so the User made the same order a second time, and UAB "Bolt Services LT" delivered the order. Considering the fact that money was deducted from the User's bank account twice, although the order was delivered to the User only once, the User demands that the money paid for the non-provided service (non-delivered order) (46.79 EUR) be returned to him.
We explain that the Office resolves disputes between consumers and sellers, service providers out of court, controls unfair terms of consumer contracts, applies legal enforcement measures, and also protects the public interest of consumers.{noformat}

{noformat}We would like to inform you that, in order to create conditions for a peaceful settlement of the dispute, the Agency has started the procedure for out-of-court settlement of the dispute between UAB "Bolt Services LT" and the User. Taking into account the claims specified in the User's request and in accordance with the aforementioned legal provisions, the Service proposes to resolve the dispute with the User peacefully and to inform the User and the Service about the decisions made no later than 11/10/2023, and if the dispute is not resolved peacefully, to provide reasoned explanations and supporting documents and other evidence regarding the circumstances specified in the User's request.
If we do not agree to resolve the dispute amicably, please inform the Service before the above-mentioned deadline: 1) indicate the reasons why the order was not delivered to the User when the User ordered it for the first time; 2) specify the reasons why the User was not refunded for the first order placed by the User when the order was not delivered; 3) submit other, in your opinion, important documents related to the investigation of the dispute, other evidence and explanations.
We note that the Office terminates the examination of the dispute if the consumer and the seller or service provider end the dispute by amicable agreement. At the request of both parties to the dispute, when the conciliation procedure is carried out, the examination of the dispute in the Office may be suspended for 60 days.{noformat}

{noformat}We inform you that the decision of the Office comes into force and must be implemented if none of the parties to the dispute files a claim in the court of general competence within 30 days from the adoption of the decision of the Office on the substance of the dispute, requesting to examine the dispute on its merits. In the event that the party to the dispute files a lawsuit in the court of general competence, it must inform the Office about it. The decision of the Office that has entered into force is an executive document. If this decision is not implemented, it can be enforced. Also, we inform you that when making a decision on the substance of the dispute, to fully or partially satisfy the claim raised by the user, the Office also decides on the seller's obligation to compensate the costs incurred by the user and the Office for handling the dispute.
Please note that the institution dealing with consumer disputes, which is ready to examine the dispute, usually examines it in accordance with the procedure of the written procedure based on the written and/or physical evidence submitted to it. When the dispute is examined by written procedure, the parties to the dispute are not invited to the meeting and the dispute is examined in their absence. In part 2 of the same article, it is noted that at the request of any party to the dispute or on its own initiative, the institution dealing with consumer disputes may decide to examine the dispute by oral procedure, when it is necessary to listen to oral explanations of the parties to the dispute or in other cases when the dispute can be better examined by oral procedure <. ..>.

[~accountid:712020:5c3f18cd-53ab-40ca-9fae-fb38035ab6d8] I kindly disagree that we push back such requests. We need to strike a balance between complying with the GDPR and cooperating with law enforcement when necessary.

 I understand that the request is not perfect from the GDPR perspective, but it states that the request is related to the investigation of “*an especially serious crime”*. Under Art. 7(5) of the Criminal Law of Latvia _“An especially serious crime is an intentional offence for which the deprivation of liberty for a period exceeding eight years or life imprisonment is provided for in this Law.”_ The consequences of the especially serious crime relate to life-threatening activities prevail over the GDPR provisions Thus, I advise [~accountid:616ff0d63e3753006f99a61c] provides data this time, but mentions that we are making an exception and in the future requests expect provision of a specific legal basis for the collection of personal data in accordance with Article 6 GDPR.

If we push back such types of requests, we will very much damage our relations with authorities. Also, we have to be aware that the practices of the state authorities are rigid and built for decades. Therefore, it cannot be changed overnight per our request. What we can do, is to numerously inform authorities about our approach and requirements, while still paying due respect to the existing practice (unless it is completely disproportional and unreasonable); gradually the practice will be changed, but not in one go, unfortunately. A softer and more cooperative approach in this transition could bring better results.

As the main concern is about tax issues (Romanian tax code) - [~accountid:712020:0b672045-ccee-47bd-a209-1bec8346b45c] I would appreciate if you can confirm.

*To summarise:*

* *the exclusion of tobacco from MOV will be allowed as long the small order fee is passed on to the fleet (related to the delivery services) and not retained by Bolt (in the latter case it could be interpreted as a mark-up to the price of cigarettes, i.e. restricted sell above the retail price)*
* *there is a risk of encouraging users to buy other products besides cigarettes in order to avoid/reduce the minimum order fee, thus tying sales, while the risk is theoretical.*

The full advice:

_“To offer some background, the advice revolves around a restriction provided in the Romanian Fiscal Code that bans retailers from selling below or above the retail price declared to authorities by the producer or importer of a relevant tobacco product._

_Excluding tobacco from MOV could generate the following two scenarios:_ 

_(i) it would generate an additional minimum order fee, which we deemed to be ok, as long as Bolt could prove that this fee is passed on to the fleet and not kept by Bolt so as to be construed as mark-up to the price of cigarettes and/or_ 

_(ii) would incentivise the buyer to buy other products in addition to cigarettes, in order to avoid/reduce the minimum order fee. This second scenario could be seen as tying, in the sense of GO 99/2000, but this is only a theoretical risk, since it may be reasonably argued that tobacco may be purchased independently, albeit paying the minimum order fee.”_

______________

[~accountid:61126e3c97981000700220ba] referring to the competition practice examples you shared below (eMAG Genius loyalty program and Mega Image campaign) - the competitors are offering a discount/benefit for a minimum value of the shopping basket, tobacco being excluded from the calculation.

* the competitors exclusion program is different from our MOV exclusion to the extent that it is actually a promotional sale from which tobacco is excluded; 
* it follows from the provisions of the Fiscal Code that if they are to apply a discount to the cigarettes retail price (by applying the same discount to the entire shopping basket), this will constitute a breach of the RO Fiscal Code - if cigarettes were to be included in the basket and a retroactive discount is applied to the entire shopping basket, then the price of cigarettes would be discounted as well (which is restricted under fiscal rules - sale below the regulated retail price), and also they will be incentivising the consumer for buying tobacco (prohibited promotion).

To my understanding, Bolt's MOV exclusion refers to any regular purchase which is not subject to a retroactive discount for the basket or any other benefit (no promotional activities).

With regards to the CCTV, the Hub should at least have cameras that are fixed on the entrances and exits; at a minimum. In terms of who should have access to the footage and how long it should be stored for; this is a question for Privacy. [~accountid:712020:0c8dd65b-46d5-4dc0-b5bd-76209c1e8048] are you able to provide some guidance in this area? Ideally we would like to have access to the footage in the event of an investigation however please clarify if that infringes on any privacy legislation.

In terms of viewing the working space, again the legality of this needs to be checked by Privacy ([~accountid:712020:0c8dd65b-46d5-4dc0-b5bd-76209c1e8048] please advise) however if it is legal, then the Local Team may install these cameras as they so wish.

Regarding your last point; here is a list of all the minimum security requirements and measures for a site like Manchester’s:

* _24/7 CCTV for the following:_
** _Main entranceway(s);_
** _Critical and/or confidential data storage areas._
* _Tamper proof alarm system monitored 24/7 by a security service provider._
** _Alarm system is to be tested annually._
* _Lockable external doors._
* _Access control into the building/working area._
* _Maintenance of a visitor register capturing the following:_
** _Name;_
** _Business purpose for visit;_
** _Confirmation of identity and business purpose by a Bolt employee; and_
** _Date and time of visit._
* _Visitors must be chaperoned throughout the building._
* _Record keeping for the following:_
** _Personnel with access to the building/workspace;_
** _Personnel holding access keys and/or cards, and with knowledge of access codes._
** _Personnel with access to areas with sensitive, critical, and/or confidential information._
* _Physically sound and secure perimeter, roof, ceilings, and flooring._



Anything that goes beyond this set of measures above is completely at the discretion of the Local Operations.

However with specific regards to the alternate/emergency exit, any alternate/emergency exits must actually *exit the building*. I am not familiar with your site layout however if it is an exit that doesn’t lead out of the building then it is not a suitable alternate exit.

Lastly, my advice would be to invest in a security guard instead of an alternate exit as that will likely be enough to mitigate any threats that have been perceived; especially in Manchester.

Please reach out if you need other information or clarity.

[~accountid:61124fbdec92ab0070270a33]the legal requirement of having direction and stop indicators  is enforceable *as of 1st July 2022 for new scooters.* 

Former scooters need to comply with new rules as of *1st January 2024.* No extra transitional period is granted under the law.

Failing to comply with technical requirements  by 1st January will expose us to the following fines and risks: 

* breach of tender commitments insofar we declared that we are fully compliant with applicable laws and regulations. Our non compliance can be flagged by users, local organisations, competitors and local authorities. This could lead to administrative fines and license termination in the worst case scenario;   
* lack of insurance coverage due to regulatory non-compliance;
* users can claim damages if the event of an accident.

* In case of orders where destination is changed by either the driver or the rider, the price of the trip is recalculated automatically based on the new route estimate. In such cases, there is no basis for a refund as there is no overcharge - the recalculation is intended behavior of the platform as the parameters of the order change.
* Yes, CS would review such cases _if_ destination change did not occur. Again, CS will manually action and refund legitimate overcharges, but this is not a case of an overcharge - the charge is appropriate, just adjusted mid-trip in response to a willing and informed decision by the client to change the destination.
* Yes - this is reflected in [public FAQs|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/support/articles/360007914159/]:
** Please keep in mind that after changing the destination, the final price may be different from the upfront or estimate price that was shown when the trip request was made

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *17th October 2023.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

* *Price paid by a rider and the pick up and drop off locations*: This data contains information about, and relates to, the third party (passenger). *Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. The reason is that order was zero preauthorized and fully covered with balance. Zero preauthorization was cancelled. Meaning that payment is cancelled while booking and booking_item are captured.

Algorithm to calculate payment status is

* if booking not captured then status is pending. Cancelled/Rejected booking statuses are not considered since such bookings are not included to the transaction history.
* if booking is captured and there is a transfer then status is finished
* if booking is captured and there is no transfer and payment is failed then status is finished
* If booking is captured and there is no transfer then status is pending (our case).

For the last item additionally we need to check whether payment is cancelled. In that case status should be finished.

Hi Antonio, I would like to make a summary of this matter and feedback provided in order to close this ticket. Below the summary of the discussions:

*GENERAL LEGAL RISKS ASSOCIATED WITH DRIVER BLOCKING*

* Blocking drivers might be seen as fulfilling criteria 2, 3, 4 and/or 5 of the ATD Law. While it seems very difficult not to control or supervise the activity of the drivers, our outside attorney advice was the following: the only way to avoid meeting those criteria is to go through the fleet and say to the fleet that a client complained about a driver so can the fleet please do something to address this issue. If the fleet doesn't do anything, the outside attorney advised that Bolt should envisage imposing a penalty first (to the fleet), and then could potentially block the fleet (not the driver) after a few events if the fleet hasn’t done anything. Disabling the driver if the fleet doesn't do it would be very risky. Based on this, *any blocking done by Bolt directly on the driver is a risk*. This is something where we are all aligned I believe.
* Below, we’re highlighting the *mitigation measures* from reclassification point of view in relation to driver blocking, starting with the strongest ones (the ones that would really help us defend ourselves in a reclassification claim) and moving down to the alternative scenarios in case the previous ones are not possible/envisageable to implement in the short term (as we understand is the case):
** *Putting in place processes allowing the fleet to block its drivers who are in breach of T&Cs, after this has been flagged by Bolt to the fleet* (in accordance with our T&Cs) - _this is the best legal solution, considering we only have an agreement with fleets and this would mean we are not at risk of meeting any ATD criteria._
** *Blocking the entire fleet in case one of its drivers is in breach of T&Cs*. _We would recommend at least to look into putting in place a process allowing us to block fleets when several of their drivers are in breach. E.g. if a fleets receives safety events on more than 50% of their drivers._
** If none of the first 2 options are developed, then it means Bolt is at risk of meeting several reclassification criteria - however, from an experience perspective, *properly informing the driver and its fleet* means that potentially we create less situations where drivers are unhappy and therefore we decrease the risks of drivers willing to sue us for reclassification - however ACT can always initiate claims and then a court would review all the facts, so such approach re: blocking might be held against us and be ruled by a court as fulfilling several criteria. In such case, we recommend that *Legal to review comms to drivers and fleets*.

*REVIEW OF THE FRAUD COMMUNICATION*

* Suspending the account for fraud in foreseen in our t&c:
** _18.7. Bolt also reserves the right to immediately_ *_suspend any access_* _in_ *_whole or in part_* _in association with Your TVDE Operator Account_ *_during the period of investigation_*_, if Bolt suspects a breach of the Agreement by the TVDE Operator, damage to Bolt's brand reputation or business, or_ *_fraudulent activity_*_._ +*_Any such suspension will be of reasonable duration and only so long as the investigation is underway._*+ _Bolt shall make use of the right described above in good faith._ *_The TVDE Operator will be informed of the reasons for this decision in a durable medium before the restriction takes effect or at the time it takes effect and will be given the opportunity to clarify the facts_* _and circumstances of the suspected breach._
** 4.8. You must not engage with or allow any fraudulent behaviour on the Bolt Platform in association with Your account. Any fraudulent behaviour in association with Your account caused or allowed by a Driver acting on Your behalf will be considered a material breach of this Agreement by You.
** 18.4… Bolt reserves the right to terminate the Agreement and suspend Your TVDE Operator Account and/or suspend any access in whole or in part in association with Your Bolt Account, without any prior notice, in the event of (i) a material or repeated breach by the TVDE Operator of any of its obligations under the Agreement and/or of any applicable laws or regulations…
* It is in particular foreseen that we may first suspend temporarily during investigation. However, applying the previous system of “warning > 3 days block > 7 days > permanent” might be seen as the exercise of disciplinary powers which is something we would like to avoid.

First off, there’s a difference between tax responsibility and contractual responsibility.

For tax purposes, the failure to issue invoices via certified software, under-declaring revenues, and submitting SAF-Ts is the responsibility of the fleets.

However, from a T&C perspective, we might be held accountable by the fleets if the tax risks materialize - for providing a service of issuing invoices in their name and on their behalf in breach of legal compliance obligations.

From my analysis, this is a summary of the risks and whether or not arising penalties can be opposed to Bolt:

!image-20231116-155712.png|width=1127,height=325!

In relation to the penalties that can be claimed by Fleets from Bolt, we should make sure that we differentiate between the non-compliance due to a Bolt error vs the non-compliance due to fleets not providing Bolt with the necessary data/tools to issue the invoices in their name in a compliant way.

And this is what I think we should safeguard in our T&C - That Bolt cannot be held responsible for non-compliance that is due to the fleet’s fault.

Hope this gives you some understanding.

and PS: this applies to Bolt Food and RH

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 20th August 2023.



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes:

* ID documentation

* Driver ride history
* Confirmation rate
* Driver dispatch preferences
* Time driver spent in status



For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data,restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,



Customer Support Team

Hi all,

I was contacted by [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] related to the question about which Bolt entity should sign the agreement with Eureka SG.

In order to address these type of questions, please note that Legal, Finance & Tax/Transfer Pricing team aligned in the past in [these guidelines|https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VB2AQBU438hOZ_TOKvoYw-VU-mGyxSe0/view].

Therefore, from my understanding of this case:

* Services covered in the agreement with Eureka SG will only relate to TH market.
* Potentially in the future these services may be expanded to other markets.

If there’s no certainty whether other markets will be involved in the future, my suggestion, following the guidelines linked above would be signing with Bolt Services TH as the services are only for TH market and from TP perspective make sense to have the related cost in that entity. 

Under this approach, if in the future other markets get involved, additional agreements can be signed with Bolt Ops (if multiple countries enters into the agreement) or the entity receiving the services (if only one, maybe Bolt Ops if the markets involved are under the so called centralized/standard model).

If we decide to go through Bolt Operations OU now, the right thing to be done from TP perspective would be Bolt Operations OU passing through the cost to Bolt Services TH. This may be straight forward now but if in the future new markets get involved, may create issues from Finance perspective. Tagging here [~accountid:5aa282eb1e5627213ac76f0e] for her to comment from Finance side, but also [~accountid:62ea2a695111209f4fde8265] in case she wants to comment anything from Tax Thailand perspective.
