please find below more details about this query. 

Pursuant to the BE Law “Labour Deal”, the relationship between the Driver and the platform is presumed being an employment contract *if 2 or 3 out of 8 criteria are met.* Some criteria have more impact than others and for those ones, 2 criteria will be enough to entail *presumption of employment*. This means that the relationship between *the platform and the Driver would be presumed to be employment, and the Driver would gain access to the applicable labour and social protection rights.* 

*Section 6 - first bullet point* (see below screenshot) p*oses a risk to the extent Bolt is restricting the possibility for the Driver to collect and use passengers' contact details to carry out transportation services outside the platform.* +*Such a restriction is likely to meet criterion no. 8 of  the Labour Deal.*+ 

The criterion at stake, ie “*Ability of building up the clientele*”, is listed among the most impactful ones. As highlighted in this [table|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YTDvwWqpw_y1ol4Upe-gGcABE7YPjfUp30l-hNgZ-qE/edit], Bolt is currently determining prices which is a sensitive matter under criterion 4.

According to our assessment, Bolt is likely to be meeting already 2/8 impactful criteria and drivers could potentially claim to be employees. 

As part of the mitigating measures to reduce the reclassification risk in BE, we kindly ask you to rephrase BE Privacy Policy in order to reduce the risk of fulfilling criterion 8. 

Basically drivers shouldn’t need Bolt’s authorisation to collect and use passengers' details - at least offline- to develop their customer base as any independent worker would do. 

Please let me know your thoughts.

Thank you again [~accountid:623c7881562ab90069f8f044] for your testing efforts, it is highly appreciated for you to get us to this point! I would like to ensure that we get clarity and alignment on this functionality. There seems to be a few overlapping topics here, so let me split this out to clarify. 

# *Order* field in Telema, is a field that populates (either through OCR automatically) or manual input by Accounts Payable Specialist the *Purchase Order (PO#)* information from the invoice. This is standard industry practice, where if we as Bolt raise a Purchase Order to the supplier, they should reflect that on the invoice they send to us. 

We currently have *two* *systems* in place, for raising Purchase Orders to suppliers. Workday and WMS. The Workday Procurement system is currently used by Rentals Procurement for the purchasing of inventory spare parts, for the micro mobility operations. WMS system is a system used by the Bolt Market team (in-house), that raises Purchase Orders which are sent to suppliers. 

{color:#ff5630}*Here, I’ll also mentioned that some of our teams are raising POs via spreadsheets with their own sequencing formats, so there is no common agreed format for Purchase Orders within Bolt. This is the most important factor that needs to be considered here please. Example for this is IOT Procurement POs, raised by Taavi. So:*{color}

Rentals SP PO = PO-EE003-23-000069 (example from invoice IN-EE003-23-009307)
WMS PO = 5527402029 (17.11.2023) (example from invoice IN-PL001-23-012968)
SS PO = ORDER# 20230616-03 (example from invoice IN-EE003-23-010369)

This means that we can have different formats of the Purchase Order numbers, that will in the end be reflected on in the *Order* field in *Telema*, which is fine as global organisations do use multiple procurement systems to meet their business needs. 

2. Request for this change ([+WD-11534+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/WD-11534]) that has been raised by [~accountid:712020:ba6cc2cb-eea3-4f5f-a454-cd7cd5d97f96] which is stating the business need for populating the *External PO Number* in Workday, with whatever data is input into the *Order field* in Telema. This code change has been developed, and tested accordingly which are proven by the tests that [~accountid:623c7881562ab90069f8f044] has executed. 

*THE LOGIC IS AS FOLLOWING:* 

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
# Order filed in Telema is populated when a supplier invoice is received.
# The invoice will be claimed, completed and approved.
# The integration will pick up the invoice and try to process it.

The integration will check the *Order* field, and if not blank, against existing POs in the system:

IF 

* Company is EE003
* PO Exists in Workday

THEN copy the lines, and populate the supplier invoice accordingly and link it to the PO in the system.

ELSE

* Company is NOT EE003
* Purchase Order does NOT exist in Workday
* BOTH

THEN only take information from Telema and populate External PO Number field.
{panel}

The key thing to note here, is that *previously* the logic for copying POs was that we would check the order number field for EE003 only, and if the PO existed then we would copy. If it it did not exist, we would return an error, to state that this is in invalid PO. Due to this requirement, we will not be able to do this anymore, in order to populate the External PO number with POs that are not existing in the Workday system. 

I would like to again advise here, since there is no *common agreed format across the organisation for Purchase Order sequencing, and this was also not part of the asked scope to build out validation against an agreed format.* 

We will await the business decision on how to proceed.

*_Automated decision-making if you are a user of the rental services_*

*What personal data do we process?*

When you use our Bolt rental electric scooters, we process your personal data collected via the sensors of the scooter to ensure you are using our services in a safe manner. The type of data we process from scooters includes geolocation data, vehicle speed, motor power (including voltage and throttle level) and driving style information (including sudden braking or skidding). This data is used to identify reckless driving events, i.e. skidding, abrupt braking, tandem riding, bad parking and collisions.

*How do we process your personal data?*

Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.

If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings:

# 

*first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehaviour;

# 

*second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and

# 

*third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.

For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

*_Automated decision-making if you are a user of the rental services_*

*What personal data do we process?*

When you use our Bolt rental electric scooters, we process your personal data collected via the sensors of the scooter to ensure you are using our services in a safe manner. The type of data we process from scooters includes geolocation data, vehicle speed, motor power (including voltage and throttle level) and driving style information (including sudden braking or skidding). This data is used to identify reckless driving events, i.e. skidding, abrupt braking, tandem riding, bad parking and collisions.

*How do we process your personal data?*

Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.

If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings:

# 

*first warning* - informs the user about the risks of misbehaviour;

# 

*second warning* - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and

# 

*third warning* - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.

For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

(SELECT

, SUM(facebook_impressions) AS facebook_impressions
, SUM(tiktok_impressions) AS tiktok_impressions
, SUM(snapchat_impressions) AS snapchat_impressions
, SUM(apple_brand_impressions) AS apple_brand_impressions
, SUM(apple_brand_cost) AS apple_brand_cost
, SUM(apple_nonbrand_impressions) AS apple_nonbrand_impressions
, SUM(google_cost) AS google_cost
, SUM(facebook_cost) AS facebook_cost
, SUM(tiktok_cost) AS tiktok_cost
, SUM(snapchat_cost) AS snapchat_cost
, SUM(costs) AS total_costs
, SUM(impressions) AS total_impressions
, SUM(total_first_time_rides) AS total_first_time_rides
, SUM(gmv_eur) as gmv
, SUM(profit_simplified_eur) as profit
, SUM(total_attributed_externals_first_time_rides) AS total_attributed_externals_first_time_rides
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_rider_measurement_lib
WHERE {geo_level} = '{geo_name}'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4) as lib

INNER JOIN

(select created_date as date_day,
'Spain' as country, 'Madrid' as city,
case when app_version like '%CA%' then 'android'
    when app_version like '%CI%' then 'ios' end as os, 
count(*) as ftr_locals
from ng_public_spark.etl_first_finished_ride_for_user
where city = 'Madrid'
and user_id in 
(select distinct id from ng_public_spark.user_user where phone_anonymized = '34')
group by 1,2,3,4) as ftr_locals

on ftr_locals.date_day = lib.date_day
and ftr_locals.country = lib.country
and ftr_locals.city = lib.city
and ftr_locals.os = lib.os{noformat}

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] , 

as promised I sat down with [~accountid:5b76bc2cb974540708ee16ee] and turns out that  unfortunately FR is not ready to launch this feature yet for the below reasons. 

+*_Commercial reasons_*+

The Rewards set up needs some adjustments to become attractive in FR: 

* due to reclass risks and regulatory constraints some rewards are not available as such in FR; 
* current Bolt Offers partnership do not allow to differentiate the offers on the different levels;
* FR Drivers are likely to dislike the rule that points will be reset month over month. FR CM suggested a validity of at least 2-3 months.

+*_Legal concerns_*+ 

From a legal perspective, the fact that the Driver is not able to freely opt-in to the program nor opt-out is not ideal. 

Besides the legal concerns already illustrated in my previous messages,  worth flagging the increased reclassification risk that may arise from the fact that we will (more or less indirectly) push Drivers to  accept rides in specific times of the day to gain more points. This will likely affect the way  drivers are providing their services  and diminish their freedom to organise their work as independent workers. To mitigate the risk,  I recommend to include the possibility for drivers to opt-out at any time if they want to.

For the time being, risks outweigh the business interest of the available rewards. Launch should be reconsidered in the future once we will have more attractive rewards such as the dynamic commission (which is being assessed for FR) and we will have a rich variety of Offers partnerships that allow differentiation depending on the ‘loyalty’ points. 

Please let me know if you are able to pass the information on to the Product Manager or if I should DM someone in particular.

Michela

The upgrade of the chat library includes a fix for a bug [CM-5232|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CM-5232] that was [reported|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CND9AL5LY/p1699030269169879] to Comms via *#dev-comms-support* channel. The bug was caused by a race condition, so it’s not reproducible 1 out of 10 (or 15) tries. However there is a scenario to reproduce it, that has been discovered from the reporter’s logs:

*Setup:*

Filter logs by {{Comms.chat}} keyword and keep them open when you reproduce the bug.

*Steps:*

# Create a first ride with a Driver.
# Finish this ride (do not cancel, but finish normally) → {{Rate your ride}} screen will appear.
# Select a rating, but do not submit it yet.
# Turn off internet on your device and quickly turn it on → Chat will start reconnecting and in the log will appear messages {{[MqttClient]: Reconnecting to a broker. Attempt #1, delay = 2000ms}}
# After a message {{Restoring the connection to a broker}} is appeared (or slightly before it) submit your last ride rating.
# When there is the following sequence of the messages in the log, it means the bug *is reproduced*:

{noformat}[MqttClient]: Reconnecting to a broker. Attempt #2, delay = 4000ms
[MqttClient]: Restoring the connection to a broker 
[MqttClient]: Disconnect from an active broker
[MqttClient]: Connected to a broker{noformat}

When it’s like this

{noformat}[MqttClient]: Reconnecting to a broker. Attempt #2, delay = 4000ms
[MqttClient]: Disconnect from an active broker
[MqttClient]: Disconnected from a broker normally{noformat}

or like this

{noformat}[MqttClient]: Reconnecting to a broker. Attempt #2, delay = 4000ms
[MqttClient]: Restoring the connection to a broker 
[MqttClient]: Connected to a broker
[MqttClient]: Disconnect from an active broker{noformat}

Then the bug *is not reproduced* and you should retry the {{steps 1 - 6}} one more time:

When the bug is reproduced:

# Create another order with a Driver.
# Open a chat with the Driver and send a few messages → Messages won’t be sent - *BUG*.
# Try to send a few messages from the Driver’s device → Messages won’t be received - *BUG*.
